value.title: Introduction to Backpropagation
value.summary: The video begins with an overview of the backpropagation algorithm, emphasizing its formal calculus foundation. It establishes the context by referencing prior content on intuitive walkthroughs and introduces the goal of understanding chain rule applications in neural networks. The discussion focuses on sensitivity analysis of the cost function to network parameters.

value.title: Single-Neuron Network and Chain Rule
value.summary: The lecture models a simple neural network with single neurons per layer, defining key components like activations (a^l), weighted sums (z^l), and the cost function C = (a^l - y)^2. It explains how the chain rule breaks down the derivative of cost with respect to weights into three parts: ∂C/∂a^l, ∂a^l/∂z^l, and ∂z^l/∂w^l, illustrating the flow of gradients.

value.title: Gradient Computation and Backward Propagation
value.summary: The video derives explicit expressions for partial derivatives, including ∂C/∂a^l = 2(a^l - y), ∂a^l/∂z^l = σ'(z^l), and ∂z^l/∂w^l = a^{l-1}. It demonstrates how these combine via the chain rule to compute gradients, and introduces the concept of propagating error signals backward through layers to update weights and biases.

value.title: Multi-Neuron Layers and Indexing
value.summary: The explanation extends to networks with multiple neurons per layer, introducing subscript indexing (k for layer l-1, j for layer l) and weight notation w_{jk}^l. It shows how the cost function generalizes to sum over all output neurons, and how the chain rule expression remains structurally similar despite increased complexity.

value.title: Error Propagation Across Layers
value.summary: The video addresses how activations in earlier layers influence the cost through multiple paths. It explains that the derivative of cost with respect to an activation in layer l-1 requires summing contributions from all downstream neurons, emphasizing the need to aggregate gradients across paths during backpropagation.

value.title: Full Backpropagation and Gradient Vector
value.summary: The lecture consolidates the process into a complete backpropagation framework, showing how gradients for all weights and biases are computed layer by layer. It highlights that the full gradient vector is built from partial derivatives across all parameters, with the chain rule serving as the core mechanism for efficient computation.

value.title: Advanced Optimization and Summary
value.summary: The video concludes with a brief overview of optimization techniques like SGD, momentum, RMSprop, and Adam, and touches on concepts such as cross-entropy loss, accuracy metrics, and gradient descent. It reinforces the importance of backpropagation as the foundational algorithm enabling neural network learning.
